{{Short description|Limit of spheres in algebraic topology}}
In [[algebraic topology]], the '''infinite-dimensional sphere''' is the [[inductive limit]] of all [[sphere]]s. Although no sphere is [[Contractible space|contractible]], the infinite-dimensional sphere is contractible<ref name=":4">Hatcher 2002, p. 19, Exercise 16</ref><ref name=":0">tom Dieck 2008, (8.4.5) Example</ref> and hence appears as the total space of multiple [[Universal bundle|universal principal bundles]].

== Definition ==
With the usual definition <math>S^n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}|\|x\|_2=1\}</math> of the sphere with the [[2-norm]], the canonical inclusion <math>\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{R}^{n+2},x\mapsto(x,0)</math> restricts to a canonical inclusion <math>S^n\hookrightarrow S^{n+1}</math>. Hence the spheres form an inductive system, whose inductive limit:<ref name=":5">Hatcher 2002, p. 7</ref><ref>tom Dieck 2008, p. 222</ref>

: <math>
S^\infty
:=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}S^n
</math>

is the ''infinite-dimensional sphere''.

== Properties ==
The most important property of the infinite-dimensional sphere is that it is [[Contractible space|contractible]].<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":0" /> Since the infinite-dimensional sphere inherits a [[CW structure]] from the spheres,<ref name=":5" /><ref>tom Dieck 2008, p. 306</ref> [[Whitehead's theorem]] claims that it is sufficient to show that it is [[weakly contractible]]. Intuitively, the homotopy groups of the spheres disappear one by one, hence all do for the infinite-dimensional sphere. Concretely, any map <math>S^k\rightarrow S^\infty</math>, due to the compactness of the former sphere, factors over a canonical inclusion <math>S^n\hookrightarrow S^\infty</math> with <math>k<n</math> [[without loss of generality]]. Since <math>\pi_k(S^n)</math> is trivial, <math>\pi_k(S^\infty)</math> is also trivial.

== Application ==

* <math>S^\infty\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{R}P^\infty</math> is the universal principal <math>\operatorname{O}(1)</math>-bundle, hence <math>\operatorname{EO}(1)\cong S^\infty</math>. The principal <math>\operatorname{O}(1)</math>-bundle <math>S^n\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{R}P^n</math> is then the canonical inclusion <math>i\colon\mathbb{R}P^n \hookrightarrow\mathbb{R}P^\infty</math>, hence <math>S^n\cong i^*S^\infty</math>.
* <math>S^\infty\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{C}P^\infty</math> is the universal [[principal U(1)-bundle]], hence <math>\operatorname{EU}(1)\cong\operatorname{ESO}(2)\cong S^\infty</math>. The principal <math>\operatorname{U}(1)</math>-bundle <math>S^{2n+1}\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{C}P^n</math> is then the canonical inclusion <math>j\colon\mathbb{C}P^n \hookrightarrow\mathbb{C}P^\infty</math>, hence <math>S^{2n+1}\cong j^*S^\infty</math>.
* <math>S^\infty\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{H}P^\infty</math> is the universal [[principal SU(2)-bundle]], hence <math>\operatorname{ESU}(2)\cong\operatorname{ESp}(1)\cong S^\infty</math>. The principal <math>\operatorname{SU}(2)</math>-bundle <math>S^{4n+3}\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{H}P^n</math> is then the canonical inclusion <math>k\colon\mathbb{H}P^n \hookrightarrow\mathbb{H}P^\infty</math>, hence <math>S^{4n+3}\cong k^*S^\infty</math>.
